question.text: A domestic corporate LP in Himalaya Arbitrage Fund has book profits of INR 20 crore for FY2025-26 and does NOT opt for Section 115BAA. Its normal-provisions tax works out to INR 2 crore. The MAT threshold under the ITA is 15% of book profits (ignore surcharge/cess for simplicity). What tax must the company pay?

answer.text: INR 3 crore (15% of book profits under MAT)
INR 2 crore (normal provisions since higher than MAT-base 0)

explanation.text: The Logic: MAT = 15% x 20 crore = INR 3 crore. Normal tax = INR 2 crore. Because MAT (3 crore) is higher than normal tax (2 crore), the company pays MAT of INR 3 crore. The INR 1 crore difference is available as MAT credit for 15 subsequent years. MAT does not apply if the company has opted into Section 115BAA or 115BAB. The Trap: Option B picks normal provisions and ignores the MAT override. Option C takes the lower of the two, which is the opposite of the rule. Option D confuses book profits with the tax payable. Note: The MAT credit can be carried forward and set off against future regular-tax liability for up to 15 assessment years, subject to conditions.
